steps.label: Understand the business
steps.goal: Separate the company’s business from this internal-tool assignment.
steps.summary: Read the company brief, then Grace’s assignment. This pilot directly serves internal staff. Explain the external business and the assistant’s responsibility separately.

questions.text: What services does the company sell?
Who does this pilot directly help?

help.direction: Separate the company’s business from this internal-tool assignment.
help.explanation: Use two sentences for the company’s services and this assistant’s users; mark uncertain background as unconfirmed.

steps.label: Users and stakeholders
steps.goal: Distinguish users, approvers and people affected.
steps.summary: Candidates are not invited users. Ask who uses the assistant, who approves and who handles exceptions. Keep opinions separate from approvals.

questions.text: Who has this problem, and who takes on extra work?
Who approves the scope and resources?

help.direction: Distinguish users, approvers and people affected.
help.explanation: One person may hold several roles. Record one responsibility to verify, then find its source.

steps.label: Validate the need
steps.goal: Make the need hypothesis open to disproof.
steps.summary: Start with one problem, supporting evidence and a possible counterexample or unknown. Check time definitions: elapsed case time is not automatically labour saved.

questions.text: How was time measured in this benefit estimate?
What evidence would make us stop?

help.direction: Make the need hypothesis open to disproof.
help.explanation: Ask about the metric’s unit, population and window. Keep unsupported benefits as hypotheses.

steps.label: Set AI boundaries
steps.goal: Specify the answer, the action and who can approve it.
steps.summary: Split a request into an answer, calculation, draft or real action. Establish human authority and available tools before choosing an approach.

questions.text: Which actions follow rules and which need retrieval?

help.direction: Specify the answer, the action and who can approve it.
help.explanation: A request can be split: retrieving a process, preparing a draft and approving it may belong to different actors.

steps.label: Solution and reference patterns
steps.goal: Compare feasible approaches; separate plans from applied settings.
steps.summary: Compare at least two substantive approaches using your triage. Reference cards describe public methods. Saving a plan does not apply settings or request resources.

questions.text: Which development work does this approach depend on?
What trade-offs are available if resources are insufficient?

help.direction: Compare feasible approaches; separate plans from applied settings.
help.explanation: Compare costs, data updates and human responsibility. Unavailable tools belong only in proposed designs.

steps.label: Evaluation, monitoring and rollback
steps.goal: Test risks against expectations and plan observation and recovery.
steps.summary: Save each expectation and its basis before running supported tests. Separate execution, quality assessments and unsupported cases. Name monitoring owners and rollback triggers.
expected_outputs: Expectations, tests and monitoring / rollback plan

questions.text: Which test is most likely to disprove this approach?
Who takes responsibility when something goes wrong?

help.direction: Test risks against expectations and plan observation and recovery.
help.explanation: Keep the basis for each expectation and name an owner for exceptions. Planned alerts are not deployed monitoring.

steps.label: Launch decision
steps.goal: Decide on exact versions and the conditions you commit to.
steps.summary: Check the exact work versions, evidence and unresolved conditions. Proceed, narrow the scope or pause; link a revision when formal feedback is ready.

questions.text: What can I commit to under these conditions?
Which changes since last time need another check?

help.direction: Decide on exact versions and the conditions you commit to.
help.explanation: Leave uncovered work visible. A submission record does not mean every judgement has been verified.
